blindSummary:
This state/province saw the country's most violent assault on a public LGBTQ event: at the 20 July 2019 equality march in its regional capital, roughly 1,000 marchers were attacked by thousands of far-right and football-hooligan groups who attempted to block the route. Police detained 25 people; 32 counter-demonstrations had been registered that day, including a prayer vigil at the main cathedral. In the run-up, the region's senior archbishop had a proclamation read in every church across the region. The surrounding county had been declared an LGBT-free zone in 2019, though the capital city itself did not adopt one, and its mayor questioned whether the march was "needed" while the governing party's city councillors filed a motion to stop it.

The protective response later shifted visibly: at the fourth equality march (28 September 2024), ~300 participants were escorted by 500 police officers and the regional police reported zero incidents — documented institutional learning under the repeated-event rule — while the 2019 pattern stands on the record: organised mass violence met with a partial 25-person detention response, embedded in a documented church-and-county mobilisation infrastructure.
